task: Read-only architecture review for SummonScout multi-client competitor-response coordination on WoW 1.12.1 / Lua 5.0. Current problem: several independent summoner WoW clients run the same addon. If one competitor public message advertises multiple destinations (e.g. Hydraxian/Hyjal/Winterspring/Silithus), every matching summoner schedules its own counter and floods the channel. Desired behavior: exactly one of our summoner clients responds to that public event with one aggregate advert like 'WTS HYDRAXIAN/HYJAL/WINTERSPRING/SILITHUS SUMMON 3G'; other clients suppress only that event and continue normal whispers/invites/summons. Aggregate price must be GUI-configurable (e.g. 3g/4g), advertised destinations must be derived safely from active configured summoner destinations, and no business should be lost for normal direct customer requests. Audit current main, focusing only on src/AddOns/SummonScout/SummonScout.lua, SummonScout_CompetitionSmartHot.lua, the HOT framework/TOC pieces needed to understand size/upvalue constraints, and any existing inter-client/master-report/control-plane primitives that could be reused. Current canonical has recently required Lua 5.0 local-declaration fixes and a 256 KiB HOT fanout repair, so explicitly avoid designs that add large closure graphs, debug.getupvalue dependence, or risky fanout growth. Determine the safest coordination mechanism between separate WoW clients (reuse existing whisper/addon/control plane if present vs minimal new mechanism), deterministic election/dedupe protocol, event identity, timeout/fail-open or fail-closed behavior, online destination knowledge, GUI ownership for group price/template, and exact integration point that avoids rewriting the core parser/scheduler. Return: (1) diagnosis of why current local cooldown cannot solve cross-client duplication, (2) evidence with exact files/symbols, (3) recommended minimal architecture, (4) race/failure cases and anti-spam behavior, (5) Lua 5.0/upvalue/file-size risks, (6) concrete tests. Do not edit. Prefer a small standalone cold-loaded coordinator module or reuse an existing control-plane if evidence supports it. Max 1000 words.
